changeSummary: Consolidates current-main platform/security foundations with homepage SSR and the six-theme experience, while introducing canonical ownership, dependency, migration and integration governance. Adds mandatory isolated identity and media policy validation gates without changing Worker routes, UI bundles or D1 schema. Adds owner-scoped reader progress API and ensures architecture/source CI runs on nested integration PRs. Adds the reader browser client integration to the existing owner-scoped reading-position API and mandatory regression coverage. Integrates owner-scoped profile and account-preference APIs and a visibility-filtered public profile projection into the same canonical Worker as reader progress.
acceptanceCriteria: Every changed repository path resolves to one registered owner
Dependency graph is acyclic and every edge points from consumer to lower-level dependency
Migration ranges are contiguous, non-overlapping and match the actual migration directory
Existing migration files are immutable; new migrations append above the base maximum
Shared surfaces require an ADR in the same PR
API and authorization evidence fingerprints match the exact Worker source
The exact PR head passes architecture, route, source, build and regression checks
Identity and media policy regressions are executed by the mandatory build.
No route, API, UI bundle, media storage binding or migration is introduced by the policy-only slice.
Reader progress API is session-owned, rate-limited and revision-guarded.
Architecture governance and Cloudflare source validation run on integration-target pull requests.
Reader browser retrieves and autosaves progress through the session-owned API.
Canonical and served versioned reader bundles remain byte-identical.
Reader progress client regression assertions execute in the existing mandatory build test.
Profile and preference APIs bind private reads and writes exclusively to the authenticated session owner.
Public profile projection excludes private account fields and discloses aggregate reading statistics only by explicit opt-in.
Profile API routes and authorization evidence are fingerprinted against the combined Worker source.
No additional migration is introduced; existing profile and preference columns are reused.
